summary: Sources describe a Pamlico Sound light station at Long Shoal (lightship 1825, screw-pile lighthouse 1867), not a fire lookout.

facts.design: Lightship from 1825, then a screw-pile lighthouse first lit May 31, 1867; a skeletal tower carried the light by 1935
facts.status_note: Lighthousefriends says no evidence of the lighthouse remains at the site today.

events.note: Congress appropriated $10,000 for a light at Long Shoal
Screw-pile lighthouse completed in spring 1867; first exhibited May 31, 1867
Thomas H. Baum becomes head keeper; in 1927 he transfers to Croatan Lighthouse
Christmas Eve storm: barges tangled around the lighthouse; Baum cuts the cable; Secretary of Commerce commends him
Light automated February 17, 1931; fog bell discontinued
Last keeper listings run to 1931; station automated
Screw-pile dwelling removed; skeletal tower displayed the automated light

corrections.why: Lighthousefriends describes a light station with a lightship, a screw-pile lighthouse and keepers. It describes no fire lookout at Long Shoal.

notes_for_editor: Probable misclassification. The record says fire lookout, but every source found describes the Long Shoal Light station. The tnlandforms list also includes non-fire structures (for example Oak Island Coast Guard, NCT222), so this entry may have come from that mixed list. Coordinates disagree: tnlandforms 35.61527,-75.83305 vs Lighthousefriends 35.556389,-75.704444, roughly a dozen km apart. Story is written as a light-station history and says so; editor should decide whether to hide or reclassify the record. Searches (2) found no fire-tower source for Long Shoal. The 1933 'skeletal tower' plan is a light structure, not evidence of a lookout. Fact-check 2026-10-21: story reworded where it copied source wording; Dare County, the 1905-1927 tenure, the Lighthouse Board replacement and the 1920 storm now each have a supporting quote.
